zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the puzzle, preserving case, spacing, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever writing attribute values into the solution JSON.
zebralogic.example: The model outputs "bob" instead of "Bob" or "pall mall" instead of "pall mall" with incorrect capitalization or missing spaces.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "X is directly left/right of Y", enforce that the house numbers differ by exactly one.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing adjacency clues that use the word "directly".
zebralogic.example: Treating "directly left of" as any house to the left, allowing a gap of more than one house.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says "X is somewhere to the left/right of Y", enforce a strict ordering (X < Y or X > Y) but not necessarily adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When handling ordering clues that do not specify "directly".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "somewhere to the left" as "directly left", thereby discarding valid positions.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the person whose child is Alice loves cooking"), link those two attributes as belonging to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue directly states that two values refer to the same entity.
zebralogic.example: Failing to link "the classical music lover" with "the Pall Mall smoker", assigning them to different houses.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., "the doctorate is in house 1"), place that attribute in the specified house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions an explicit house number.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring a clue that says "Arnold is not in the first house" and placing Arnold in house 1.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Before final output, ensure the JSON object is syntactically valid: proper brackets, commas, quotes, and no trailing commas.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Immediately before emitting the final solution JSON.
zebralogic.example: Producing JSON with a missing closing brace or an extra comma after the last element.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with any reasoning before it, so the verifier can parse it correctly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When constructing the final output for a puzzle.
zebralogic.example: Putting the JSON before the reasoning block, causing the verifier to miss the answer.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B, B = C), propagate the links so all linked attributes are assigned to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After gathering all equivalence clues, before solving the placement.
zebralogic.example: Linking A = B and B = C but leaving C unlinked from A, resulting in contradictory assignments.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between two entities, enforce that the absolute difference in their house numbers is N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing distance clues such as "two houses between".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "two houses between" as a difference of two instead of three, placing the entities too close.

zebralogic.title: ReasoningLengthControl
zebralogic.principle: Keep reasoning concise enough to stay within token limits; avoid overly verbose enumerations that could cause the final JSON to be truncated. Summarize constraints and place the solution JSON at the very end.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When solving a puzzle with many clues or when the response is approaching the model's token budget.
zebralogic.example: The model writes a long, detailed step‑by‑step reasoning that exceeds the token limit, causing the final JSON to be cut off or omitted.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting "N houses between" as "N houses apart" (using a difference of N instead of N+1).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats "between" as a simple distance rather than accounting for the houses that lie in between, forgetting the +1 offset.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions "N houses between", add one to N to compute the required absolute house-number difference.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to generate text after the JSON, so the verifier stops parsing before the complete solution.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Emit the JSON as the very last part of the output and stop generating further text.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the final answer to be truncated.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model includes overly long reasoning or repeats clues, pushing the total response beyond the allowed token budget, which cuts off the trailing JSON.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Limit the length of reasoning, summarize clues instead of verbatim listing, and ensure the solution JSON fits comfortably within the remaining token budget.
